questions.prompt: A trajectory is evaluated with ATE. Why is a rigid alignment applied first?
options: It converts radians into degrees, so that the estimate and the reference share the same units.
The world origin and orientation are a free choice not observable from images, so alignment removes that gauge.
Alignment is needed only for lidar, since camera trajectories are always in the world frame.
Alignment lowers the noise of the camera, so the remaining error shows only the algorithm's accuracy.
questions.explanation: Images cannot fix the global frame; alignment removes only that freedom.

questions.prompt: A robot drives a 40 m loop and ends 2.678 m from the start. What is the drift as a percentage of path length (2 decimals)?
questions.skillLabel: Drift as a percentage of path length

questions.prompt: Heading bias of 0.01 rad is added at each of 40 steps of a square loop. What total heading error (rad) accumulates by the end?
A heading bias gives RPE of 0 over one step but large RPE over 40 steps. The best explanation is
options: The local translation per step is unchanged, but the errors accumulate over longer intervals.
RPE ignores translation, so only rotation errors can make it grow with the interval.
The trajectory was not aligned first, so the interval error is dominated by the offset.
The metric is broken, because a zero value over one step cannot occur on real data.
questions.explanation: Heading bias rotates later motions in the world frame; the per-step translation in its own frame is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Pose composition for a planar robot must express the delta motion in
options: image coordinates, since the motion is measured from the camera
an arbitrary frame chosen separately for each step of the trajectory
the robot's current frame, rotated into the world by theta
the world frame, since all poses are stored there and deltas can be added directly
questions.explanation: x += cos(th) dx - sin(th) dy etc.

questions.prompt: A robot at pose (0,0,pi/2) moves delta (dx,dy,dth) = (1,0,0) in its own frame. What is the new world y coordinate?
Explain what loop closure adds to visual odometry, and give one way a false loop closure can occur and one safeguard.
rubric: States that a loop closure is a constraint between two distant poses that reduces accumulated drift.
Names perceptual aliasing (similar-looking places) as a cause of false closures.
Names a safeguard such as geometric verification or robust optimisation.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
